reasons: Lake identity is verified as Neil v. Biggers, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1972-12-06, year 1972.
Lake citations match the asserted official cite 409 U.S. 188, parallel cites 93 S. Ct. 375 and 34 L. Ed. 2d 401, and vendor-neutral cite 1972 U.S. LEXIS 6.
Cached opinion text header also shows 409 U.S. 188 (1972), Supreme Court of United States, decided December 6, 1972.
The opinion is centrally about due-process limits on eyewitness identification evidence from a station-house showup.
The opinion states that general guidelines emerge from prior identification cases and then formulates the totality/reliability factors, supporting a refinement role.
The lake record lists 4347 indexed citing opinions and a treatment scope note identifying Biggers as the source of the five reliability factors, supporting the Key/Progeny aspect.
residual_risks: The exact corpus taxonomy for the label Key — Progeny / Refinement is not defined in the disclosed files, but the disclosed opinion and lake record support the label's substance.

reasons: The opinion says the police had not exhausted comparable-person options but that the evidence need not therefore be excluded.
The opinion frames the central question as whether, under the totality of the circumstances, the identification was reliable even though the confrontation procedure was suggestive.
After applying the reliability factors, the Court found no substantial likelihood of misidentification and held the evidence properly allowed.
residual_risks: The holding would be more precise if it included the opinion's no substantial likelihood of misidentification formulation and removed the dangling ellipsis.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Even identification evidence from an unnecessarily suggestive confrontation is not automatically excluded; under the totality of the circumstances, it may be admitted if reliable and there is no substantial likelihood of misidentification.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A, so no independent treatment finding is raised.

residual_risks: No Lens A treatment audit performed; Lens B owns treatment/currency.
